q.en: A chocolate costs ₹10 today. Prices rise 6% a year. In 10 years it will cost about…

explain.en: 6% a year, compounded for 10 years, makes ₹10 into about ₹18.

q.en: A ₹7,500 phone is "only ₹699 a month for 12 months" plus a ₹1,200 fee. What do you pay in total?
Someone wants to pay you ₹1,500 on UPI. What do you need to enter?

options.en: Nothing. Just share your UPI ID

explain.en: You never enter a PIN to receive money. A PIN only sends money out.

q.en: A lender charges "₹2 per ₹100 per month". What is that per year?

explain.en: ₹2 every month for 12 months is ₹24 per ₹100: 24% a year.

q.en: A scheme promises to double your money in one year, guaranteed. It is most likely…

explain.en: Doubling in a year is 100% returns. Nobody honest can guarantee that.

q.en: You keep ₹1,000 in a tin box for 5 years while prices rise 6% a year. What happens?

explain.en: The notes stay ₹1,000, but prices rise about 34% in 5 years. It buys less.

q.en: "Only ₹999 a month for 15 months" for a ₹12,000 phone. How much extra do you pay?

explain.en: ₹999 × 15 = ₹14,985. That's ₹2,985 more than the phone's price.

q.en: A "buyer" sends a QR code and says, "Scan and enter PIN to receive your money." What happens if you do?

explain.en: Scanning a QR and entering a PIN always pays out. It's a scam.

q.en: You need ₹20,000. Which is usually the cheapest?

explain.en: The moneylender is 24% a year on the full amount; apps and cards cost even more. The SHG is 12%.

q.en: Which matters most for long-term savings growth?

explain.en: Time lets compounding work. Starting small and early beats starting big and late.
